rituals.hook: Catch the moment an unplanned thought begins.
rituals.play:
Rest on one plain point.
When a thought appears, catch its first beat before you follow it.
rituals.twist: Name only its type — word, image, memory, plan, body feeling — then release.
rituals.reveal: You catch the thought before it fully forms.
rituals.mindBend:
A thought can arrive before you choose it.
Catch the moment an unplanned thought begins.
rituals.safety:
Use only one everyday thought.
If you start trying to force a blank mind, stop
and look at a real object nearby.

rituals.safety:

If the exercise shifts into trying to force a blank mind, end
there.
Allow your thoughts to move normally again.

rituals.hook: Let one word in.
rituals.play:

When the first word appears, hold it for two beats.
Do not finish the sentence.
rituals.twist: If the arrival is an image, wait for its first word.
rituals.reveal: One word stays one word.
rituals.mindBend:
A sentence is built word by word.
It does not arrive as one finished block.
Let one word in.
rituals.safety:
Limit this to one everyday thought.
If the exercise shifts into trying to force a blank mind, do
not continue.
Return to everyday thinking.

rituals.hook: Let one thought end there.
rituals.rule: The first thought is allowed in full.
rituals.play:
Let one thought finish.
For five seconds, do not add a reason, defence, guess, or replay.
rituals.twist: A truly unrelated thought may enter.
rituals.reveal:
The thought ends.
The chain does not.
rituals.mindBend:
The first thought is not the loop.
Let one thought end there.
rituals.safety:
Keep this to everyday thoughts.
When hard-to-stop thought checking appears, step out and move back
to everyday activity.

rituals.hook: Put many thoughts into a one-by-one line.
rituals.rule: Only one item can occupy the front slot.
rituals.play:
When several thoughts compete, imagine numbered tickets.
Process only the lowest number for three beats.
All others wait silently.
rituals.twist:
After three beats, move the front ticket to the back without solving
it.
rituals.reveal: Competition becomes an orderly sequence rather than a pile-up.
rituals.mindBend:
Maybe overload is not too many thoughts.
Put many thoughts into a one-by-one line.
rituals.safety:
Choose everyday thoughts.
When getting stuck on the thought appears, end the round.
Do something simple and concrete.

Pop only the newest item from awareness.
rituals.safety:
Use one brief thought for one pass.
If you start trying to force a blank mind, stop
and let your mind continue normally.

but not the change in change.

on paper
or screen.

If risk is acute, avoid being left alone until appropriate support has
taken over.

rituals.hook: Put risky action tools out of reach.

Give keys, cards, a phone, or other risky action tools to a
trusted person
or move them out of reach.
rituals.reveal: Impulsive action becomes harder.
rituals.mindBend: Less access to risky tools changes what can happen next.
rituals.safety:

Hand over or secure only items that can be managed safely.
Bring in a trusted person if judgement or impulse control is badly
reduced.

rituals.hook: Do not drive if you may be unsafe.
rituals.play:
If you may be impaired or medically unwell, do not test your
driving.
Hand over the keys.
rituals.reveal: Driving risk drops.
rituals.mindBend:
A no-drive rule protects you when your own judgement may be
impaired.
rituals.safety:
This is a hard safety boundary: if you may be impaired, highly
destabilised,
severely sleep-deprived, intoxicated, or otherwise unsafe to drive,
do not test yourself behind the wheel—use another transport option.

rituals.hook: Support basic needs without ignoring warning signs.
rituals.rule: Medical concerns still need medical help.
rituals.play:

when needed.
rituals.reveal: Basic care happens alongside real assessment.
rituals.mindBend: Simple body care can help comfort without answering a medical question.
rituals.safety:
This can support basic comfort but must not be used to explain
away concerning symptoms.
Simple hydration never substitutes for medical assessment when red flags are present.

rituals.hook: Move to a quieter safer place.

rituals.twist: Keep attention on the outside world.

rituals.safety:
Move to a place that is truly safer, not only quieter.
If the setting is unsafe, too intense, or full of risky cues,
choose a staffed or supported place.

rituals.hook: Hand the assessment to a professional.

Share three facts: what is happening, when it started, and what makes
it risky.
rituals.reveal: Assessment moves to qualified support.

over assessment.
rituals.safety:

Give the facts to a qualified professional and follow their real-world
assessment.

rituals.hook: Step away from the high-risk cue.
rituals.play:
Move away from the gambling, drug, alcohol, weapon, or other high-risk
cue.
Seek support.
rituals.twist: Do not bargain with the cue.
rituals.reveal: The cue is farther from the action.
rituals.mindBend: Leaving the risky setting removes part of the cue system itself.
rituals.safety:
This requires real distance from the high-risk environment.
Do not linger near the cue to prove you can resist it,
and bring in support if leaving safely is difficult.

scary

rituals.reveal: Time and company lower pressure to act now.
rituals.mindBend: Time with another person changes both isolation and decision pressure.
rituals.safety:
This is supervised delay for non-urgent action.
Choose a genuinely safe companion and do not use waiting to postpone
emergency care
or another time-critical safety step.

rituals.hook: Check one fact with two outside sources.
rituals.play:
Pick one safe present fact, such as time or location.
Check one source, then a second source or trusted person.
rituals.twist:
If they disagree or you still feel unsafe, stop and seek human
or professional support.
rituals.reveal: Two outside sources support one present fact.
rituals.mindBend: Two separate sources agreeing is stronger than repeating one source.
rituals.safety:
This counts only when the sources are truly separate and reliable.
If safety is involved, use a qualified person or service instead of
repeated checks.

indecision.

to crisis,

and do not leave to test whether you can manage the danger
alone.
